title: PRD: Hosted Interaction Bundles — compact lanes and acceptance checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers want a single hosted endpoint that can express a compact set of behaviors (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) while enabling predictable cost/latency tiers and deterministic embedding contracts for downstream similarity and reranking. Current product surface exposes separate endpoints or large, policy-heavy endpoints that increase cognitive load and operational risk.

Goal: Ship a PRD and launch checklist for a new "Interaction Bundle" concept: small composable lane definitions (Fast/Text/Embed/Rerank) that map to curated model+quantization profiles, routing policies, and eval suites. The bundle should be easy for SDKs and Console to present as a single consumable "profile" and support safe fallbacks and rollouts.

Scope: Draft includes API surface changes (bundle id + lane selector), behavioral contracts per lane (determinism, tokens limits, embedding cosine normalization), rollout and canary plan, operational metrics to instrument, and acceptance criteria/eval harness. Excluded: new model training, Dedicated capacity contract changes, enterprise-only RBAC gating (handled in separate ticket).
tasks: Finalize lane behavioral contracts for Fast/Text/Embed/Rerank
Define API fields: bundle_id, lane, quality_band, fallback_policy
Create eval suites (50 prompt sets) and target pass/fail thresholds
Implement server-side routing prototype and synthetic traffic tests
Update SDKs (python/ts) to accept bundle shorthand
Console UX: bundle selector + per-lane telemetry view
Create canary plan and rollback criteria
Draft public docs + migration guide for customers
acceptance_criteria: API: bundle_id + lane accepted by hosted endpoints and documented in spec
Behavior: Embeddings lane must produce normalized vectors (L2=1 +/- 0.02) across model variants
Determinism: Text lane with seed and deterministic=true returns identical tokens for 95% of eval prompts
Latency: Fast lane p95 <= 120ms on standard small requests under baseline 500 RPS synthetic load
Cost: Compact lanes show <= 15% token-cost overhead vs baseline optimized single endpoint (measured on test tenants)
Rollback: Canary triggers if quality regression > 5% or error rate > 1% over 15 minutes
Telemetry: Console displays per-lane token counts, cost breakdown, and per-bundle health metrics
Docs: Public PRD, API reference, and migration guide published and linked from Console
notes: Trade-offs: Bundles simplify customer UX at the cost of additional routing logic and a larger model-variant catalog. We optimize by restricting initial launch to 3 variant families and two quantization profiles.
Decision: Use cosine-normalized embeddings contract for downstream reranking to avoid consumer-side normalization drift.
Fallback policy: default fallback is model-variant warm-switch; soft-fallback to higher-latency but higher-quality model configured per-bundle.
Privacy: No customer data retention changes; embeddings are not stored by default (subject to tenant opt-in).
Open question: whether to expose lane-level custom parameters (e.g., allow_custom_top_k) in 1.0 or gate to enterprise only. Proposed: gate in 1.1.
